b_rows_sample.anchor: Concept relationships — the reviewer's example chain, validated ... KnowledgeOS creates PKS contains Engineering Knowledge organized by Ontology used by Capabilities executed through Runtime produces Evidence improves KnowledgeOS
b_rows_sample.statement: The proposed chain is validated edge by edge: 'KnowledgeOS creates PKS' is a hypothesis (n=0, every PKS is authored by a person); 'PKS contains Engineering Knowledge' is WRONG, violating I-7 (a PKS contains product knowledge and bindings; reusable method must not live in it — the current breach is the exception that proves the rule); 'knowledge organized by Ontology' holds with the precision that L-A organizes artifacts/carriers, not knowledge itself (I-1); 'used by Capabilities' holds (capabilities may read across space boundaries, never own — H-1); 'Capabilities executed through Runtime' is imprecise (capabilities are advisory scripts invoked on demand; the runtime executes Execution Assets/ASTs; 41 enforced controls live runtime-side while every capability is advisory — the drawn edge hides this finding); 'Runtime produces Evidence' should attribute production to WORK (P-7/P-8), the runtime only hosts the work; 'Evidence improves KnowledgeOS' is only partly true (n≈3 informal, B-1's fact).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Two corrections to the Addendum's own positioning ... "KnowledgeOS is a Core Domain" ... Contradicts a DA ruling
b_rows_sample.statement: Two corrections to an Addendum's positioning: (1) 'KnowledgeOS is a Core Domain' contradicts AIP-14/DA ruling 2026-07-27 that the Election System is the Core Domain and the platform is a Supporting Subdomain; the Reference Model records only the conditional (engineering knowledge would be Core Domain if the gate opened, and it has not). (2) 'PKS is a generated projection' was falsified last round: existing PKS artifacts carry Status: ACCEPTED WITH REFINEMENTS, a Commission, and ARB endorsement 9.9/10 — they are authored, not derived.

b_rows_sample.anchor: W-3 · "PKS is a projection" — FALSIFIED for every existing PKS artifact
b_rows_sample.statement: The claim 'PKS is a projection' is falsified for every existing PKS artifact: examined fields (Authority: Generated, human-asserted; Status: ACCEPTED WITH REFINEMENTS; a Disposition History with ARB reviewer endorsement 9.9/10; a Commission) are incompatible with a projection, which would carry authority:derived (machine-checkable), no acceptance (regenerated, not accepted), a source and regeneration command, and no Commission. A mechanical grep for authority:derived|generated across docs/pks, docs/knowledgeos, docs/implementation returns 10 files, every one a prose mention of the vocabulary, not an application of it — those paths sit outside knowledge-schema.yaml's declared scope.include. This sharpens a prior Ontology Classification finding ('blocked in practice') to stronger: existing PKS artifacts are positively authoritative — authored, commissioned, reviewed, disposed, and accepted — incompatible with 'derived'.

b_rows_sample.statement: D-7's 'Context Type' claim (one PKS instance per product) was inferred from a single instance (PublicDigit's), with zero instances generated from the type; 'one instance per product' is an observation of one case restated as a rule — a type never instantiated is a description, not a discovered construct.

b_rows_sample.statement: Per-domain confidence after falsification (R16 Strong/Medium/Weak scale): D-1 Strong->STRONG; D-2 Strong->MEDIUM; D-3 Strong->WEAK; D-6a (Evidence Protocol) new->MEDIUM; D-6b (Product Evidence) new->STRONG; D-5 (Engineering Capability, not a context) Medium->MEDIUM (unchanged, H-CAT-1 stands); D-4 (Workflow, rejected) ->STRONG as a rejection; D-7 (PKS, a context type) new->WEAK. Distinction drawn: falsified is worse than unevidenced — D-3 and D-7 carry contradicting evidence (falsified); D-6a carries no evidence (unevidenced).

b_rows_sample.statement: Fifteen candidate concerns, each citing its supporting commission and what it waits on: K-1 dimensional-with-archetypes meta-model; K-2 the archetype set (strong: DOMAIN/PROCESS/CAPABILITY/KNOWLEDGE/ARTIFACT/RUNTIME ASSET/PROJECTION; weaker: CONTAINER; weakest: PURPOSE); K-3 the four partial orders (authority, production, realization, containment); K-4 11 invariant relationships vs 8 implementation choices; K-5 DP-n as capability anchor; K-6 Knowledge Space = declared boundary+owner+constitution; K-7 authority = provenance x standing, four progression kinds; K-8 the strategic domain set PD-1/2/3/5; K-9 viewpoints as presentation; K-10 decision-readiness as the platform's product; K-11 FREEZE/RETIRE as insufficiency evidence; K-12 PKS extends context-engineering with governance; K-13 the canon-track reference artifacts themselves; K-14 the mission is enacted via 8 artifacts; K-15 ownership splits (candidate-unowned=ladder working, operating-unowned=defect, sole instance Runtime Adapter).

b_rows_sample.anchor: The six concepts ... MISSION · ENGINEERING KNOWLEDGE · ENGINEERING CAPABILITY · ENGINEERING ARTIFACT · PRODUCT KNOWLEDGE SPACE · PRODUCT
b_rows_sample.statement: Six concepts defined by responsibility/lifecycle/owner/dependencies, none defined by a folder: MISSION (why the platform exists; enacted->candidate->ratified, currently enacted-unratified; owner: sponsor; depends on nothing, the root); ENGINEERING KNOWLEDGE (rules/methods/decisions that transfer between products; ES-006.1 ladder; owner DA for policy, sponsor+ARB for method; depends on MISSION); ENGINEERING CAPABILITY (protect exactly one invariant; observed->...->promoted; shape frozen under PGP-01..05; depends on MISSION+KNOWLEDGE); ENGINEERING ARTIFACT (carry knowledge in a representation, never the knowledge itself; statuses.yaml 8 states lint-enforced; owner field; depends on KNOWLEDGE); PRODUCT KNOWLEDGE SPACE (hold one product's concepts/language/contexts/bindings; authored today, generated as hypothesis n=0; owner product team; depends on KNOWLEDGE method + PRODUCT subject); PRODUCT (deliver business value; own delivery lifecycle; owner product team; depends on PKS + CAPABILITY).

b_rows_sample.anchor:
skip Candidate->Accepted rejected : PASS (I-12 covering relation)
  in-order promotion                : PASS (history ['Candidate', 'Supported', 'Accepted'])
  10^6 evidence, no authority act   : PASS (not committed)
  authority act crosses boundary    : PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Executed checks confirm: a status ladder (Candidate -> Supported -> Accepted) enforces a strict covering relation (I-12) -- skipping Candidate directly to Accepted is rejected, and in-order promotion succeeds; a Committed decision boundary is reachable only from Accepted and requires an authority act, with evidence volume alone (even 10^6 items) never sufficient to cross it (A6/I-4); adjacent FA layered states (REJECTED/CONFLICTED) are reachable only by a governed act (never silently) and are preserved with their reasoning in history rather than deleted.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
target state: Acceptance=Accepted AND Contest=Active (008 §11, board case)
  layered-model options: stay 'Accepted' (contest invisible) or move to
  'CONFLICTED' (acceptance suspended). NO single state carries both.
  -> PF-6 residue CONFIRMED as an expressibility fact
b_rows_sample.statement: An expressibility probe against a source model Omega_A = (Support, Acceptance, Commitment, Contest), targeting the state 'Acceptance=Accepted AND Contest=Active' (a real board case, source 008 section 11), finds no single state in the layered model can carry both facts jointly: the only options are to stay Accepted (making the contest invisible) or move to CONFLICTED (suspending acceptance). Confirmed as an expressibility fact, not itself judged good or bad, and named the PF-6 residue.

Reference implementation of the status ladder: Item.promote() enforces the I-12 covering relation by raising ValueError on any non-adjacent transition (e.g. Candidate directly to Accepted); Item.commit() enforces that the Committed boundary is reachable only from Accepted status and only given a non-None authority_act parameter, with an evidence_volume parameter present but functionally inert (never checked against any threshold); Item.governed_move() enforces that adjacent FA states (REJECTED, CONFLICTED) require a non-None governed_act parameter and appends a reasoned history entry rather than mutating status silently, so prior states are preserved rather than deleted.

type_signature.domain: an Item in one of {Candidate, Supported, Accepted, Committed(purpose), REJECTED, CONFLICTED}

b_rows_sample.anchor: The ratified architecture's mathematical content is honest but thin ... The formal-object layer is signatures without constructions.
b_rows_sample.statement: The ratified architecture's load-bearing mathematics is limited to a small, honest set: two pipeline-level evidence invariants (I-5, I-6), a three-element covering relation plus one boundary edge (I-12/A6), a conjunction law for decision admissibility, a structured non-scalar non-metric gap operator (Zero), and a stratification loop -- all mathematically sound as stated and independently reproduced by the audit's own reference implementations, none of them deep mathematics, none pretending to be. By contrast, the formal-object layer is signatures without constructions: eta (EC derivation), Learn (state dynamics), the ladder's transition calculus, the policy-version transition calculus, the r-to-P typing map, and identity/equality criteria for the model's own objects (evidence equivalence, state equality, frame equivalence) are all named and typed only at the arrow level, never constructed -- the book discloses this wherever it is governed to (OQ-1, OQ-3, OQ-4, AF-F-3/4), and this audit adds members the existing registers did not yet carry.

Ω_A = ( SupportStatus, AcceptanceStatus, CommitmentStatus, ContestStatus ) ... NotAccepted ≠ Rejected and Unresolved ≠ Rejected — insufficiency is not refutation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the source (Step 008) six-outcome acceptance function alpha_rho:EAxPxC->{Candidate,Supported,Accepted,Rejected,Contested,Unresolved}, explicitly non-linear (Supported+Contested is a legitimate joint state), and the source's own recommended multidimensional status Omega_A=(SupportStatus,AcceptanceStatus,CommitmentStatus,ContestStatus) with a worked institutionally-accepted-yet-epistemically-contested instance, plus the two boxed inequalities NotAccepted!=Rejected and Unresolved!=Rejected.

b_rows_sample.statement: Executing EXP-4 shows that taking the mean of an ordinal epistemic-status ladder (Candidate/Supported/Accepted) under three admissible (order-preserving) numeric encodings produces different PROCEED/no-PROCEED verdicts for the same portfolio, demonstrating the mean is not a meaningful (Roberts-admissible) operation on an ordinal scale; min, max and median are shown to be invariant controls.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Resolution SHALL be forward-only: the conflict record SHALL survive resolution
b_rows_sample.statement: Constitution v1.0 Article 8, clause 3 (verbatim, line 92) requires only that the CONFLICTED record survive resolution; it does not name a destination rung. A textually available but unsupported 'ordinal monotonicity' reading would require an L1 article to constrain an L2 rung ordering the Constitution never names, against the ratified layer-separation rule -- the two readings (record-preservation vs destination-rung) are formally distinguished (FORMAL-DERIVED) as prior open decision Z-1.

b_rows_sample.statement: Verdict: no textual contradiction found between A6 and Articles 3/4/7/8/9/11; three decision items remain open (R-1 A6's exhaustiveness as the sole authority-crossing rule; R-2 whether an L1 article may constrain an L2 rung ordering the Constitution never names; the Y-5 provenance question) plus P-2 (the CONFLICTED return rung), which Article 8.3 does not settle on the reading its own text supports.

a_rows_sample.statement: Restates AgentBehavior ≠ EngineeringKnowledge as foundational, splitting the Agent layer (operating mechanics) from the KnowledgeOS layer (engineering knowledge/governance).

a_rows_sample.statement: Presents the target architecture diagram: KnowledgeOS shared at the top, Claude and Codex agents as specialized harnesses beneath it feeding Engineering Work.

a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 1: duplicated authoritative architecture knowledge across .claude/memory/ and .codex/memory/ creates DivergenceRisk; result FAIL — an important named failure mode the architecture must avoid, requiring pointer/index/agent-state directories rather than competing authoritative stores.

a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 2: an agent-behavior instruction in .claude/ correctly stays classified as AgentPolicy, not organizational knowledge; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 3: an engineering architecture rule (hexagonal architecture requirement) existing only inside .claude/ is a KnowledgeBoundaryViolation; result FAIL — the rule must live in KnowledgeOS and be referenced, not embedded solely in agent configuration.

a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 9: Codex cannot inherit a developer's approval authority merely by being asked, absent explicit delegate authorization; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Steps 101-105 established the conformance model for architecture, semantics, governance, agents. Step 106 asks: does that architecture survive contact with the actual running system? A_I->A_C->A_D->A_R. Crucial requirement: A_R approx A_I subject to explicitly documented runtime differences.
b_rows_sample.statement: Frames Step 106's central test: whether the architecture survives contact with the running system, via A_I(intended)->A_C(implementation)->A_D(deployed)->A_R(runtime), requiring approximate conformance A_R≈A_I subject to documented differences.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.1 — Why runtime is the final authority for runtime facts ... Documentation ≠ RuntimeEvidence.
b_rows_sample.statement: States Documentation ≠ RuntimeEvidence: runtime is the final authority for runtime facts, illustrated by a documented ServiceA→ServiceB call diverging from actual production topology.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.2 — Four representations ... Architecture model A_I, Source model A_C, Deployment model A_D, Runtime model A_R. The goal is not necessarily literal equality. It is Conformance(A_I,A_C,A_D,A_R).
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the four representations (Architecture/Source/Deployment/Runtime models) and states the goal is Conformance(A_I,A_C,A_D,A_R), not literal equality.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.3 — Experiment 1: deployed version mismatch ... Architecture says KnowledgeOS=2.1. Deployment runs KnowledgeOS=2.0. Expected: DeploymentDrift. Result: PASS. The system must report the mismatch rather than silently assuming the latest code is running.
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 1: a deployed version (2.0) lagging the architecture-declared version (2.1) is DeploymentDrift, which must be reported not silently assumed away; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.4 — Experiment 2: configuration mismatch ... Repository defines FeatureX=True. Production configuration FeatureX=False. Expected: runtime behavior must be evaluated using the actual configuration. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 2: runtime behavior must be evaluated using the actual production configuration (FeatureX=False), not the repository default; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.5 — Configuration is architecture ... Architecture is not only SourceCode. It includes relevant Configuration. A_R=Code+Configuration+Infrastructure+Dependencies+RuntimeState.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.6 — Experiment 3: environment-specific architecture ... Development: PostgreSQL. Production: ManagedDatabase. Expected: not automatically a violation if the architecture explicitly allows environment-specific infrastructure (ArchitectureRule=EnvironmentAware). Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 3: environment-specific infrastructure (dev PostgreSQL vs prod ManagedDatabase) is not automatically a violation if declared EnvironmentAware; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.7 — Runtime topology ... Component→Instance→Environment→Host/Platform. e.g. AgentGateway→Container→Production→Cluster.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the runtime topology model Component→Instance→Environment→Host/Platform.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.8 — Experiment 4 ... Architecture identifies AgentGateway. Runtime has AgentGateway_1 and AgentGateway_2. Expected: both instances map to the same logical component. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 4: multiple runtime instances (AgentGateway_1, _2) must map to the same logical component; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.9 — Logical versus physical identity ... LogicalComponent ≠ RuntimeInstance. A component may have n instances.
b_rows_sample.statement: States LogicalComponent ≠ RuntimeInstance: one component may have many runtime instances.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.10 — Experiment 5 ... A deployment scales ServiceA: 2→8 instances. Expected: architecture does not become eight separate logical components. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 5: scaling ServiceA from 2 to 8 instances does not create eight logical components; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.11 — Runtime dependency discovery ... evidence may come from network connections, service discovery, traces, logs, configuration, deployment manifests.
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists evidence sources for runtime dependency discovery: network connections, service discovery, traces, logs, configuration, deployment manifests.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.12 — Experiment 6 ... Architecture says A ↛ C. Runtime trace shows A→C. Expected: RuntimeArchitectureViolation. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 6: an observed A→C dependency violating the architecture's A↛C rule is RuntimeArchitectureViolation; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.13 — Runtime architecture graph ... G_R(t)=(V_R,E_R) where V_R=RuntimeComponents, E_R=ObservedDependencies. Then compare with G_I.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the runtime architecture graph G_R(t)=(V_R,E_R), compared against the intended graph G_I.

b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Drift(t)=Difference(G_I,G_R(t)), called one of the most valuable KnowledgeOS capabilities.

b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 7: an undocumented new external API appearing in production is a DriftCandidate; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.16 — But drift is not automatically violation ... A runtime difference may be ApprovedException or ExpectedDynamicBehavior. Drift ≠ Violation.
b_rows_sample.statement: States Drift ≠ Violation: a runtime difference may be an ApprovedException or ExpectedDynamicBehavior.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.17 — Experiment 8 ... A temporary scaling mechanism creates additional runtime instances. Architecture does not enumerate every instance. Expected: no architecture violation. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 8: temporary scaling instances not enumerated in architecture is not itself a violation; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.18 — Dynamic architecture ... Instances(t), Load(t), Connections(t), ResourceAllocation(t). KnowledgeOS must model which dimensions are Static versus Dynamic.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires KnowledgeOS to model which architectural dimensions are intentionally dynamic (Instances(t), Load(t), Connections(t), ResourceAllocation(t)) versus static.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AgentAuthority ⊆ DelegatedAuthority.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the autonomy boundary: an agent may possess technical capability greater than its permitted authority, which is acceptable only if the enforcement boundary prevents unauthorized action (AgentAuthority ⊆ DelegatedAuthority); distinguishes four non-interchangeable concepts Capability, Permission, Delegation, Authority, illustrated by an agent having kubectl-delete credentials (Capability=True) while governance sets ProductionDelete=False (Authority=False) — the agent must not treat the credential as authorization.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A2: Technical capability MUST NOT be interpreted as organizational authority.
a_rows_sample.statement: Adds agent-specific constitutional rule A2 ('technical capability MUST NOT be interpreted as organizational authority'), stated as complementary to C2 (Authority); notes autonomy is action-specific rather than agent-wide — RunArchitectureCheck can often be autonomous while Finding->ChangeProductionArchitecture may require human authority.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A0 — Read ... A6 — Change organizational authority
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a seven-level autonomy-class scale for agent actions: A0 Read/inspect, A1 Analyze/reason over evidence, A2 Verify/execute deterministic checks, A3 Recommend/propose action, A4 Execute reversible low-risk action within explicit delegation, A5 Execute governed production action requiring explicit delegated authority, A6 Change organizational authority requiring explicit human/organizational governance; worked through experiments A1-A5 (read=ALLOW; run tests=ALLOW if tool access permitted; create remediation proposal=ALLOW since a proposal is not yet an organizational decision; merge to protected production branch=DENY without explicit delegation [A4/A5]; modify the KnowledgeOS Constitution itself=A6, DENY without constitutional authority).

b_rows_sample.anchor: G0 Governance exists only in documents ... G6 Governance closes the runtime feedback loop.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a seven-level Governance maturity ladder G0-G6 (documents only -> indexed documents -> registered decisions -> decisions with authority/provenance/lifecycle -> decisions connected to implementation -> decisions connected to deterministic verification -> closed runtime feedback loop) and requires establishing whether governance concepts are represented as first-class KnowledgeOS semantic objects or merely documents/processes.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K0 Documents ... K6 Continuously verified knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a seven-level Knowledge maturity ladder K0-K6 (documents -> searchable -> structured -> governed -> evidence-linked -> machine-traversable -> continuously verified), with K6 as the approximate target and the current level to be reconstructed by evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A0 Standalone AI tool ... A6 Continuously assured agent.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a seven-level Agent maturity ladder A0-A6 (standalone tool -> repository-aware -> knowledge-aware -> governed -> evidence-producing -> authorized-action -> continuously assured), estimating current Claude/Codex architecture as beyond A1 but requiring evidence to establish the exact level.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AgentCapability ≤ GovernanceAssurance
b_rows_sample.statement: States the crucial architecture-gap risk: A5 agent capability paired with only K2 knowledge maturity is dangerous (AgentCapability > KnowledgeAssurance creates architectural risk), formalizing the design principle AgentCapability ≤ GovernanceAssurance — the more powerful the agent, the stronger the surrounding governance/evidence architecture must be; worked example — an agent that can Read+Write+Deploy while KnowledgeOS only knows Documents+Search means the agent can act faster than the organization can establish what should be true, 'unacceptable for governed engineering.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Level 0 Files ... Level 6 Governed autonomous engineering. Maturity = f(Governance,Knowledge,Evidence,Assurance,Agent,Traceability).
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a seven-level architectural maturity ladder (Level 0 files scattered, Level 1 structured artifacts with known locations/formats/conventions, Level 2 registry with stable identities/metadata, Level 3 governance integration, Level 4 evidence integration, Level 5 Assurance Graph with cross-context relationships/traceability/historical reconstruction, Level 6 governed autonomous engineering Context->Reasoning->Authorization->Action->Evidence->Verification); argues maturity is multi-dimensional (Maturity=f(Governance,Knowledge,Evidence,Assurance,Agent,Traceability)) since a platform may be Level 5 in deterministic assurance but Level 2 in knowledge authority — not a single number, distinct from the earlier per-dimension G0-G6/K0-K6/A0-A6 ladders (S1031).

a_notations: A2: capability MUST NOT be interpreted as authority

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels share the notation 'A0..A6'

a_rows_sample.anchor: AAG=(V,E) ... V=V_C∪V_K∪V_I∪V_E∪V_T∪V_F
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Architecture Assurance Graph AAG=(V,E) with node types V_C (components/bounded contexts), V_K (contracts), V_I (invariants), V_E (enforcement mechanisms), V_T (verification tests), V_F (evidence/artifacts), and typed edges Component-owns->Invariant, Contract-carries->SemanticProperty, Mechanism-enforces->Invariant, Test-verifies->Invariant, Evidence-supports->Test/Claim.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I -> Owner -> Mechanism -> Test -> Evidence
a_rows_sample.statement: For a critical property I, the complete assurance chain is I->Owner->Mechanism->Test->Evidence; a missing edge is potentially an assurance gap. Worked example: I_Authority->Governance->AuthorizationPolicy->NegativeTest->TestEvidence is a complete chain.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A — Defined and enforced ... D — Claimed but unverifiable
a_rows_sample.statement: Every invariant is classified into one of four situations: (A) defined and enforced and verified; (B) defined but not enforced (M=empty); (C) implemented but not architecturally declared (a mechanism exists but nobody established which invariant it protects); (D) claimed but unverifiable (documentation asserts I=True but no evidence exists). D is flagged as particularly dangerous.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Gap(I)=RequiredAssurance(I)-ActualAssurance(I) ... Gap(I) in {None,Low,Medium,High,Critical}
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines assurance gap conceptually as Gap(I)=RequiredAssurance(I)-ActualAssurance(I), explicitly refusing to assign arbitrary numerical values and instead classifying into {None,Low,Medium,High,Critical} 'until we establish a justified scoring model'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Component correctness =/=> System correctness
a_rows_sample.statement: An architecture may have every individual bounded context (Evidence, Assessment, Governance) correct while still having a critical global assurance gap, e.g. if the contract Assessment->Governance silently drops uncertainty; boxed conclusion: component correctness does not imply system correctness.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assurance(I_global) <= min{Assurance(I_1),Assurance(I_2),...}
a_rows_sample.statement: States a weakest-link property: for a critical end-to-end property I_global, assurance is bounded by the minimum assurance of its constituent links, explicitly qualified as 'not a universal mathematical law; it is a useful conservative assurance model' — if one indispensable boundary lacks a provenance guarantee, end-to-end provenance cannot be honestly claimed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Traceability_syntactic=True but Traceability_historical=False
a_rows_sample.statement: Decision traceability example D->A->E: traceability is only True if each reference (Decision->Assessment ID->Evidence ID) remains resolvable and semantically versioned; if the Assessment ID resolves only to the latest Assessment, syntactic traceability can hold while historical traceability fails — 'this distinction is crucial'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SyntacticCorrectness =/= SemanticCorrectness ... HTTP 200 ... JSON schema valid
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes SyntacticCorrectness != SemanticCorrectness: an HTTP 200 proves transport success but not BusinessMeaningCorrect; a valid JSON schema does not prove SemanticContractValid.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A=(A_s,A_m,A_e,A_t,A_p,A_g)
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a candidate six-dimension KnowledgeOS assurance vector A=(A_s,A_m,A_e,A_t,A_p,A_g): A_s structural (component exists, boundary explicit, dependencies controlled, contracts defined), A_m semantic (meaning preserved, no overloaded concept, no Boolean replacing a richer state), A_e epistemic/statistical (evidence, inference, assumptions, uncertainty, correlation vs causation, model version), A_t temporal (which version/policy/model applied when, historical reconstructability), A_p provenance (claim origin, traversable chain), A_g governance (who was authorized, under which valid policy, permission vs execution).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Vector assurance is preferable to premature scalarization
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues a single global assurance score is dangerous: if A_s=1 but A_p=0, a scalar like 0.83 could falsely imply reasonable assurance, whereas for critical systems one missing indispensable property may be enough to block certification; boxed principle: vector assurance is preferable to premature scalarization — an explicit statistical-design principle.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C0 — Informational ... C4 — Critical assurance
a_rows_sample.statement: Provisionally classifies invariant criticality into five levels: C0 Informational (documentation/style), C1 Functional (normal business behavior), C2 Semantic (meaning/context preservation), C3 Governance (authority/policy/compliance), C4 Critical assurance (safety, irreversible action, high-impact decision, legally significant state); flagged as needing later validation against real KnowledgeOS use cases.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Mechanism(I)=f(Criticality(I))
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes assurance-mechanism selection as a function of criticality: low-risk -> Documentation+UnitTest; medium -> IntegrationTest+ContractTest; high -> PropertyBasedTest+Replay+AuditEvidence; critical -> FormalModel/Proof where practical — self-labeled 'a proposed framework, not yet a frozen standard'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A=(InputRef,ModelRef,InstructionRef,Output,Uncertainty,Validation,Provenance)
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes an AI-generated-artifact metadata schema A=(InputRef,ModelRef,InstructionRef,Output,Uncertainty,Validation,Provenance), stating the schema must be derived from the actual KnowledgeOS implementation but conceptually AI output should not be treated as an unexplained opaque fact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AI -> CandidateResult -> DeterministicValidation -> AcceptedArtifact. Not: AI -> ProductionTruth
a_rows_sample.statement: States the architecture must route AI output through AI->CandidateResult->DeterministicValidation->AcceptedArtifact, never directly AI->ProductionTruth, calling this distinction 'central to our KnowledgeOS design'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: TrustedFor(x,p,t) ... Valid(x,Context,Time,Purpose)
a_rows_sample.statement: Warns against another bare Boolean (`trusted = true`); trust/assurance must be contextual, TrustedFor(x,p,t) — an artifact trustworthy for Task_1 need not be trustworthy for Task_2. Generalizes to Valid(x) being usually incomplete; the better form is Valid(x,Context,Time,Purpose), called 'a major insight for KnowledgeOS': validity is not absolute but ValidForPurpose(P).

a_rows_sample.anchor: StructuralValid ... SemanticValid ... EpistemicallyValid ... TemporallyValid ... GovernanceValid
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes five validity types (Structural/Semantic/Epistemic/Temporal/Governance Valid), concluding Valid(x) should be treated as shorthand only when the intended dimension is explicitly known.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Different missing edges represent different classes of architectural weakness
a_rows_sample.statement: States the missing-node principle: Invariant->Owner with no Enforcement is a design gap; Enforcement->Test missing is an assurance gap; Test->Evidence missing is an auditability gap — different missing edges are different classes of architectural weakness, letting the architecture 'diagnose itself' via forall I_i: Complete(AAG(I_i))? producing a reproducible gap report.

a_rows_sample.anchor: System -> Output + EvidenceOfCorrectness
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the architecture's strongest form as System->Output+EvidenceOfCorrectness rather than merely System->Output, stated as precisely what deterministic assurance is trying to accomplish.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We should not claim: 'The architecture is mathematically proven.' ... FormalizableArchitecture
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit self-warning: the architecture must not be claimed as mathematically proven; what exists is a FormalizableArchitecture, and the next task is determining which portions can actually be Formalized->Specified->Verified.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ### DDD ... VERY STRONG ... Gītā 1–4 ... DEEP CONSISTENCY
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 211 verdict: DDD, Mathematics, Statistics, Governance, and AI are each rated VERY STRONG, and Gita chapters 1-4 rated DEEP CONSISTENCY, citing continued distinctions Identity!=State, Knowledge!=Action, Capability!=Authority, PastState!=CurrentState, Decision!=Outcome.

b_rows_sample.anchor: each file's tail contains the agenda for the next step
b_rows_sample.statement: Structural observation, load-bearing for the whole verification: each file in the 208-215 band ends with the agenda section for the *next* step (e.g. the file titled 'Step 208' ends with a '# Step 209' section at line 1423 onward), so the band is a chain of overlapping documents and every 'Step N' agenda exists in two places (as the prior file's tail and the next file's own opening).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Cardinality drift: the 8-set I_KOS is silently superseded by a 15-list I1-I15 without amendment
b_rows_sample.statement: Probe (c-iii): Step 209 Section 209.42 boxes and freezes an 8-member invariant set I_KOS = {I_identity, I_version, I_provenance, I_temporal, I_epistemic, I_authority, I_decision, I_execution}. Step 210 Section 210.25 then tabulates 15 invariants I1-I15 with no mapping given between the 8 and the 15. Independently checked: I13 (illegal transitions rejected) and I14 (preconditions/postconditions) have no member of I_KOS to belong to, and I15 (no semantic strengthening) is likewise unhoused unless forced into I_epistemic. The 8-set is silently superseded by the 15-list without amendment; only Step 209's own caveat ('we should not freeze this yet') prevents this from being an outright contradiction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: POPULATED. 60 of 60 cells filled. ZERO '?', ZERO TBD. THE ALL-'?' PATTERN IS BROKEN.
b_rows_sample.statement: Probe (d): Step 210's 15-row invariant-verification matrix (lines 809-825) has 60 of 60 cells filled with zero placeholders -- a real, material departure from the corpus's prior pattern (Steps 108, 112, 114, 116, 121 all used all-'?' matrices), credited as a genuine corpus-level improvement.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The matrix realizes 3 of the 6 tuple components it is supposed to instantiate
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 Section 210.1 boxes V_i = (I_i, O_i, E_i, M_i, T_i, F_i) (invariant, owner, enforcement mechanism, monitoring mechanism, test/verification, failure behaviour) but the rendered matrix has only 4 columns (ID, Invariant, Owner, Verification) realizing I_i, O_i, T_i -- E_i (enforcement), M_i (monitoring), and F_i (failure behaviour) are absent for all 15 invariants: 45 of the declared tuple components are unrealized. Enforcement is the one component that would distinguish an architectural property from an architectural principle, the exact distinction Step 210's own boxed opening claim rests on.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Verification column contains test NAMES, not test RESULTS
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 210's Verification column lists 15 test names verbatim (identity transition test, version reconstruction, lineage traversal, semantic contract test, negative inference test, payload/semantic test, reproducibility test, privilege-path test, failure simulation, outcome verification, conflict test, historical replay, state-machine test, invariant test, transformation test) with zero results, zero of the fifteen tests existing as code, and none run (confirmed by Part 2's zero-executable-fences finding). Under TEST SPECIFIED != TEST EXECUTED: 15/15 specified, 0/15 executed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DDD CATEGORY ERROR IN THE 'Owner' COLUMN
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 206 Section 206.15 derives the candidate bounded-context set as Observation, Evidence, Assessment, Governance, Decision, Execution. Step 210's Owner column instead contains values like 'Domain' (a layer), 'Persistence/Domain' (two layers), 'Knowledge infrastructure' (a layer), 'Assessment/Contracts' (half artifact-kind), 'Aggregate' (a tactical pattern, not a party), and 'Contracts' (an artifact kind). Only 4 of 15 invariants (I5, I7, I8, I12) have a single, named bounded-context owner; seven (I1, I2, I3, I11, I13, I14, I15) have an owner entirely outside the derived context set, making them ownerless invariants under Step 212's own Section 212.15 criterion; five (I2, I4, I6, I9, I10) have slash-shared owners, Step 212's own Section 212.16 shared-ownership problem.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step 210's matrix instantiates, in 12 of its 15 rows, the two failure modes Step 212 names two files later — and neither file notices
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 212 Section 212.15 warns explicitly against 'Ownerless Invariants' (I exists but Owner(I) = empty set), yet Step 212 Section 212.4 reprints the same 15 invariants from Step 210 with the Owner column deleted entirely, and performs no such search -- discarding the exact data (Step 210's Owner column, with 7/15 ownerless and 5/15 shared) that would have triggered Step 212's own diagnosis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Further arithmetic checks: 0.87>=0.80 correct; 0.91+/-0.08 within range at 1 sigma but 2-sigma bound exceeds 1; ratio checks disclaimed
b_rows_sample.statement: Additional independently-verified arithmetic in the band: Step 209 Section 209.15's 0.87 >= 0.80 evaluates to True (correct). Step 208 Section 208.14 / Step 210 Section 210.12's 0.91 +/- 0.08 gives [0.83, 0.99], within [0,1] at 1-sigma, but at 2-sigma the upper bound is 1.07 > 1 -- out of range for a quantity called 'confidence', though the corpus never commits this specific error since the interval's coverage level is left unlabelled. Step 215 Section 215.24's ratios (182/43=4.233, 43/17=2.529, 17/8=2.125, 8/4=2.0, total 45.5x) make no arithmetic claim and are correctly disclaimed as unknown. b_rows_sample.anchor: PREVIOUS DEPENDENCY: 1 (Step 208 only); LATER RESPONSE: Step 210 replaces I_KOS with I1-I15 without amendment
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 cites exactly one prior step (Step 208) and zero prior invariant families. Later response in scope: Step 210 Section 210.25 replaces the 8-member I_KOS with a 15-row I1-I15 without amendment; Step 210 Section 210.9 restates Step 209's Section 209.25 semantic-strength principle as Strength(T(x))>Strength(x) requires Justified(T); Step 212 Section 212.4 reprints I1-I15.

b_rows_sample.anchor: FORMAL OBJECTS: Architectural Principle != Architectural Property; V_i=(I_i,O_i,E_i,M_i,T_i,F_i); Referential Integrity < Semantic Historical Integrity
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 ('Invariant Verification Matrix') defines a 6-tuple V_i=(I_i,O_i,E_i,M_i,T_i,F_i) per invariant; boxes 'Architectural Principle != Architectural Property' and 'No claim of architectural compliance without identifiable evidence'; defines Reachable(D,E)!=empty; boxes 'Referential Integrity < Semantic Historical Integrity' and 'Epistemic state cannot be silently strengthened'; states Strength(T(x))>Strength(x) requires Justified(T); boxes 'Quantitative value without relevant uncertainty may constitute semantic loss'; defines a statistical-result 8-tuple A=(theta-hat,Estimator,Sample,Population,Model,Assumptions,Uncertainty,Validity); boxes 'Documentation < ExecutableEvidence < FormalProof'; a conceptual Assurance(I)=f(Evidence,Coverage,Independence,Repeatability,Criticality); an E_1..E_5 evidence hierarchy (documentation..formal verification); the target for-all-s-in-S_reachable: I(s)=True; and boxes 'AI may assist assurance; AI should not be the sole source of assurance', plus the 15-row invariant-verification matrix itself (60/60 cells filled).

b_rows_sample.anchor: LATER RESPONSE IN SCOPE: Step 211 reverses Test/Evidence order; Step 212 drops the Owner column and recalibrates E_n
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 cites only Step 209 by number ('up to Step 209, we have asked...'). Later response: Step 211 Section 211.2 restates the assurance chain with Test before Evidence, contradicting Step 210's own Section 210.40; Step 212 Section 212.4 reprints I1-I15 minus the Owner column; Step 212 Section 212.6 re-mints an E_0..E_5 scale with different rung definitions than Step 210 Section 210.30's E_1..E_5.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EVOLUTION/DEFINITION VERDICT: CLEAR on the principle/property distinction, CONTRADICTORY on E_1..E_5 (twice)
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 answers 'where' (role names) and 'how proven' (test names) but not 'is it true' for any invariant. CLEAR: the principle/property distinction (its best contribution), Referential Integrity < Semantic Historical Integrity, the three assurance levels. INCOMPLETE: V_i is 6-ary, only 3 components ever instantiated. AMBIGUOUS: 'Owner' is used as bounded context, layer, pattern, and team interchangeably. CONTRADICTORY: E_1..E_5 vs Step 212's E_0..E_5 (Contradiction #3), and E_1 bound to two incompatible types within Step 210 itself (Contradiction #4: Section 210.20's evidence-item E_1 vs Section 210.30's documentation-rung E_1).

b_rows_sample.anchor: FIRST INVALID INFERENCE: Section 210.30 vs 210.20 (E_n ambiguity); honest gaps in 210.26/210.28/210.29
b_rows_sample.statement: Section 210.20 uses E_1⇒P and E_2⇒¬P as evidence items; Section 210.30, ten sections later, binds E_1=documentation...E_5=formal verification as evidence-strength levels -- the same subscripted symbol carries two incompatible types with no disambiguation, and every downstream use of E_n in Steps 212-214 inherits the ambiguity. Section 210.29 honestly declines to scalarize Assurance and names fake precision (Assurance=97.3%) as a hazard, yet Section 210.28 immediately prior writes Critical(I)⇒HigherAssurance(I), a comparison requiring the very ordering Section 210.29 declines. Section 210.26 correctly concedes a test provides evidence, not proof (Test(I_8)=PASS does not prove I_8=True in all states), then Section 210.32's target for-all s in S_reachable: I(s)=True leaves S_reachable undetermined (Section 210.33 concedes this openly) -- an honest, correctly-labelled gap, not an invalidity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: COMPUTABILITY: highest rung reached is INPUTS_KNOWN, for I_i/O_i as strings only; 15 tests specified, 0 run
b_rows_sample.statement: V_i is DEFINED with 3/6 components at INPUTS_KNOWN (role-name granularity); the I1-I15 matrix is DEFINED->INPUTS_KNOWN (names) but not CONSTRUCTIBLE (no mechanism/code/test); Assurance(I) is DEFINED but explicitly barred from numeric evaluation; S_reachable is DEFINED but conceded as the open challenge, not CONSTRUCTIBLE. The highest rung reached anywhere in Step 210 is INPUTS_KNOWN, and only for I_i and O_i as strings. TEST VERDICT NOT_EXECUTED: 15 tests specified by name, 0 written, 0 run; Section 210.16's negative test ('can an AI-generated Assessment directly invoke an execution command? Expected: False') is designed in prose and never run against anything.

b_rows_sample.anchor: STATISTICAL VERDICT: STRONG (the 8-tuple A=(theta-hat,...,Validity) is the best statistical section in the band); two correct refusals and two measurement violations
b_rows_sample.statement: Section 210.13's 8-tuple statistical result A=(theta-hat,Estimator,Sample,Population,Model,Assumptions,Uncertainty,Validity) is correct and genuinely good statistical practice, rarely done in architecture documents, but never carried into the matrix (which collapses all eight back into one row) and never connected to the corpus's prior statistical steps (025N, 074, 082, uncited). Correct refusals: Section 210.29 declines to scalarize Assurance (names fake precision explicitly); Section 210.27's Documentation<ExecutableEvidence<FormalProof is a properly-used ordinal. Violations: Section 210.28's Critical(I)⇒HigherAssurance(I) compares assurance levels the same file declines to scale; the E_1<...<E_5 ladder (Section 210.30) is re-issued by Step 212 Section 212.6 with different rung contents and an added E_0 -- the same ordinal scale has two incompatible calibrations in the band, making any statement 'we have E_2 evidence' uninterpretable without knowing which file it was written under -- a scale-integrity failure that silently corrupts later aggregation. The 15-row matrix itself carries no scale at all (purely nominal, no arithmetic attempted -- correct).

b_rows_sample.anchor: DDD VERDICT: MIXED — strong distinctions (Architectural Principle != Property; Referential Integrity < Semantic Historical Integrity; Memory/Identity/History split), weak ownership
b_rows_sample.statement: Architectural Principle != Architectural Property is exactly the right DDD-governance move; Referential Integrity < Semantic Historical Integrity (Section 210.5, a foreign key proves existence not that this version was the artifact used) is a real and useful insight; Section 210.39's Memory/Identity/History separation, concluding the current domain object need not carry all history internally, is correct DDD (event sourcing / separate read model), well argued. Against this, the Owner column's category error means only 4/15 invariants have a single bounded-context owner, 7/15 are owned by a layer or pattern (which cannot be accountable), 5/15 are slash-shared, and I13/I14 are owned by 'Aggregate' -- a tactical pattern name is never the answer to 'who is accountable' in DDD.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ASSUMPTIONS / HIDDEN ASSUMPTIONS / UNDEFINED SYMBOLS — Step 210
b_rows_sample.statement: Stated: each invariant has exactly one owner; a test name determines a test; enforcement can be located by inspection. Hidden: that the 15 invariants are the right 15 (no derivation from I_KOS's 8, no completeness claim); that S_reachable is finite or tractable (required by the for-all quantifier, false for unbounded state); that Owner and Enforcement are separable -- the matrix drops Enforcement and keeps Owner, implicitly assuming Owner=Enforcement, which Step 211 Section 211.29 later denies ('Invariant->Owner present but Enforcement missing = a design gap'), meaning by Step 211's own criterion all 15 rows of Step 210's matrix are design gaps. Undefined symbols: Justified(T), Strength(x), Critical(I), HigherAssurance(I), Coverage/Independence/Repeatability, S_reachable, Estimator/Sample/Population/Validity, DA's codomain Result.

b_rows_sample.anchor: WHAT SURVIVES / WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE — Step 210, including the word 'Matrix' itself
b_rows_sample.statement: Survives: Architectural Principle != Architectural Property; Referential Integrity < Semantic Historical Integrity; Documentation<ExecutableEvidence<FormalProof; the 8-component statistical result tuple; the refusal of test-as-proof; the refusal to scalarize assurance; the Memory/Identity/History split; the 15 invariant names as a working checklist. Does not survive: the Owner column (11/15 rows unusable); the Verification column as evidence of anything (0/15 executed); V_i as a realized 6-tuple (3/6 realized); E_1..E_5 as a stable scale; and the word 'Matrix' in the title -- a 4-column table realizing 3 of 6 declared dimensions, with no status and no results, is a checklist.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The most damaging collision is E-binding #2 vs #5, which occurs INSIDE ONE FILE (Step 210)
b_rows_sample.statement: Of the twelve distinct bindings of the glyph E catalogued across the band, the most damaging collision is internal to a single file: Step 210 Section 210.20 writes E_1⇒P (an evidence item entailing a proposition), and Step 210 Section 210.30, ten sections later, writes E_1=documentation (the weakest rung of an assurance ladder) -- same symbol, same file, incompatible types, no disambiguation, no notice.

b_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 uses I exclusively for an information measure (I(E), I(A), I_required, I_preserved); Step 209 onward uses I exclusively for invariants (I_L, I_C, I_S, I_i, I_identity, I1-I15, I(s)). The rebinding is never announced -- a reader comparing I(C(A)) (Section 208.4, information) to I(s)=True (Section 210.32, an invariant predicate) is reading two different symbols under one glyph.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 106 established A_I→A_C→A_D→A_R. Step 107 asks: when these four differ, what exactly does the difference mean? Not every difference is a defect.
a_rows_sample.statement: Frames Step 107's question: what a discrepancy in A_I/A_C/A_D/A_R actually means, since not every difference is a defect.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 107.1 — The central principle ... We must never automatically conclude A_I≠A_R ⇒ ArchitectureWrong. Instead Difference→Classification→Decision.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the central principle: A_I≠A_R does not automatically mean ArchitectureWrong; instead Difference→Classification→Decision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 107.2 — Six possible explanations ... D1 Architecture defect (A_I old→new), D2 Implementation defect (A_C≠A_I), D3 Deployment defect (A_D≠A_C), D4 Runtime defect (A_R≠A_D), D5 Authorized deviation (A_R≠A_I but AuthorizedDeviation=True), D6 Unknown (EvidenceInsufficient). This sixth state is essentia
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines six mutually exclusive discrepancy categories D1-D6 (architecture defect, implementation defect, deployment defect, runtime defect, authorized deviation, unknown/insufficient evidence), with D6 called essential.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 107.3 — Experiment 1: architecture obsolete ... A later approved architecture decision replaces B with C. Runtime: A→C. Expected: not a runtime violation. The architecture model is outdated. Result: D1 — Architecture evolution.
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 1: runtime A→C reflecting an already-approved architecture change (B replaced by C) is classified D1 — Architecture evolution, not a runtime violation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 107.4 — Experiment 2: implementation defect ... Architecture says A↛Database. Source code contains A→Database. No exception exists. Result: D2 — Implementation defect.
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 2: source code containing a forbidden A→Database connection with no exception is classified D2 — Implementation defect.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 107.5 — Experiment 3: deployment defect ... Source contains Version=5.0. Production runs Version=4.9. Result: D3 — Deployment drift.
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 3: production running an older version (4.9) than source (5.0) is classified D3 — Deployment drift.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 107.6 — Experiment 4: runtime defect ... Correct version is deployed. Configuration is correct. Runtime nevertheless opens a forbidden connection. Result: D4 — Runtime violation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 4: a forbidden connection opened despite correct version/configuration is classified D4 — Runtime violation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 107.7 — Experiment 5: authorized deviation ... Architecture requires DatabaseA. A temporary migration exception authorizes DatabaseB until 2026-12-31. Runtime uses B. Result: D5 — Authorized deviation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 5: runtime using DatabaseB under an authorized temporary exception (valid until 2026-12-31) is classified D5 — Authorized deviation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 107.8 — Experiment 6: insufficient evidence ... Architecture says A→B. Repository evidence is incomplete. Runtime traces are unavailable. Result: D6 — Unknown. We must not invent the answer.
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 6: incomplete repository evidence and unavailable runtime traces yield D6 — Unknown, with the answer explicitly not invented.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 107.9 — Why this classification matters ... Mistake A: change documentation to match reality (A_I:=A_R), which can hide defects. Mistake B: declare runtime nonconformance without understanding intentional changes. Both are dangerous.
a_rows_sample.statement: Names two dangerous mistakes the classification model prevents: silently redefining A_I:=A_R (hiding defects) and declaring nonconformance without recognizing legitimate intentional changes.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 107.10 — Architecture drift object ... Drift=(Expected,Observed,Difference,Evidence,Classification,Impact,Authority,Validity,Resolution).
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the full Drift object Drift=(Expected,Observed,Difference,Evidence,Classification,Impact,Authority,Validity,Resolution).

type_signature.codomain: Difference x Classification x Impact x Authority x Validity x Resolution

a_rows_sample.anchor: 107.11 — Expected versus observed ... ExpectedState and ObservedState. Delta=Observed-Expected.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Delta=Observed-Expected as the measurable difference between ExpectedState and ObservedState.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 107.12 — Experiment 7 ... Expected Replicas=4. Observed Replicas=3. Delta=-1. Expected: a measurable drift finding. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 7: Replicas=4 expected vs 3 observed gives Delta=-1, a measurable drift finding; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 107.13 — Semantic drift ... Architecture still calls something 'Repository.' But the implementation now represents 'Knowledge Source.' That can indicate a bounded-context or ubiquitous-language problem.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines SemanticDrift: architecture terminology diverging from actual implemented meaning, indicating a possible bounded-context/ubiquitous-language problem.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 107.14 — Experiment 8 ... Code uses KnowledgeItem but its semantics have evolved into DecisionRecord. Expected: potential semantic drift. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 8: a KnowledgeItem class whose actual semantics have evolved into DecisionRecord is potential semantic drift; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 107.15 — Governance drift ... GovernanceRule ≠ ImplementedControl. Rule: all production changes require approval. Implementation allows direct production deployment. Expected: GovernanceDrift.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines GovernanceDrift: a stated rule (approval required) diverging from the actually implemented control (direct deployment allowed).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 107.16 — Agent drift ... KnowledgeOS says Claude→KnowledgeOS. But .claude/ contains an independent copy of authoritative architecture knowledge. Expected: AgentBoundaryDrift.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines AgentBoundaryDrift: .claude/ accumulating an independent authoritative-knowledge copy diverging from the intended Claude→KnowledgeOS pointer relationship, extending Step 105's agent-boundary concerns.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 107.17 — Experiment 9 ... .codex/ begins accumulating its own authoritative architecture rules. Expected: potential divergence from KnowledgeOS. Result: PASS — drift detectable.
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 9: .codex/ accumulating its own authoritative rules is potential divergence, detectable as agent drift; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 107.18 — Security drift ... Expected Agent↛ProductionDB. Observed Agent→ProductionDB. Expected: SecurityDrift. This may be higher severity than ordinary architecture drift.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines SecurityDrift (an observed forbidden Agent→ProductionDB connection), noted as potentially higher severity than ordinary drift.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 107.19 — Configuration drift ... Expected PolicyMode=Enforced. Observed PolicyMode=Permissive. Expected: ConfigurationDrift.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines ConfigurationDrift, e.g. PolicyMode observed as Permissive against an expected Enforced.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We have now reached the point where the reconstruction must become empirical. Conceptual Reconstruction→Evidence Extraction. The objective is to construct the actual graph G_actual=(V_actual,E_actual) from the existing KnowledgeOS/EKS material.
b_rows_sample.statement: States Step 116's shift Conceptual Reconstruction->Evidence Extraction, aiming to construct the actual graph G_actual=(V_actual,E_actual) from existing material.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 116.1 — The extraction rule ... No architectural relationship is accepted merely because it is desirable or conceptually logical. Claim_architecture⇒Evidence_implementation. If evidence is missing: Status=UNKNOWN. Not Status=FALSE.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the strict extraction rule Claim_architecture⇒Evidence_implementation, defaulting missing evidence to Status=UNKNOWN, never Status=FALSE.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 116.2 — Evidence hierarchy ... E0 No evidence, E1 Terminology, E2 Static implementation, E3 Behavioral evidence, E4 Verification evidence, E5 Runtime evidence, E6 Governance evidence. E0<E1<E2<E3<E4<E5<E6.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a seven-level evidence hierarchy E0 (no evidence) through E6 (governance evidence).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 116.3 — Node extraction ... SemanticObject: ID, Type, Meaning, Representation, Owner, Lifecycle, Authority, Provenance, EvidenceLevel, Source.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the SemanticObject node-extraction schema with ten fields (ID/Type/Meaning/Representation/Owner/Lifecycle/Authority/Provenance/EvidenceLevel/Source).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 116.4 — Relationship extraction ... SemanticRelationship: Source, Target, Type, Direction, Evidence, Confidence, Status. Evidence_42-supports->Decision_17. The evidence must demonstrate both the relationship and its meaning.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the SemanticRelationship edge-extraction schema (Source/Target/Type/Direction/Evidence/Confidence/Status), requiring evidence for both relationship and meaning.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 116.5 — First graph layer: implementation graph ... G_I=(C,D,I) where C=components, D=dependencies, I=interfaces. This is the result of Step 111.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the implementation graph G_I=(C,D,I), the result of Step 111.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 116.6 — Second graph layer: data graph ... G_D=(Data,Relations). Entities, tables, documents, records, metadata, events, indexes, caches.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the data graph G_D=(Data,Relations) over entities/tables/documents/records/metadata/events/indexes/caches.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 116.7 — Third graph layer: semantic graph ... G_S=(Concepts,SemanticRelations). The important point is: G_I≠G_D≠G_S. They are related graphs.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the semantic graph G_S=(Concepts,SemanticRelations), stating G_I≠G_D≠G_S as related but distinct graphs.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 116.8 — Fourth graph layer: governance graph ... G_G=(Actors,Authorities,Decisions,Policies). This allows us to ask: Who is allowed to establish or change this knowledge?
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the governance graph G_G=(Actors,Authorities,Decisions,Policies), enabling the question of who may establish or change knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 116.9 — The combined model ... Governance Graph → Semantic Graph → Data Graph → Implementation Graph. This layered representation is more accurate than trying to force everything into one architecture diagram.
b_rows_sample.statement: Presents the four-layer stack (Governance->Semantic->Data->Implementation) as more accurate than forcing everything into one architecture diagram.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 116.10 — Experiment 1: component → semantic concept ... EvidenceRepository. What semantic concept does it represent? Evidence, Document, Artifact, Observation. We do not infer the answer from the class name alone. Result: requires semantic evidence
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 1: an EvidenceRepository component's actual semantic concept (Evidence/Document/Artifact/Observation) cannot be inferred from class name alone, requiring semantic evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 116.11 — Experiment 2: table → domain object ... knowledge_items table. If it contains content, embedding, source URL, chunk number, it may actually represent IndexedDocumentChunk. The database name alone is insufficient. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 2: a knowledge_items table containing content/embedding/source-URL/chunk-number fields may actually represent IndexedDocumentChunk, since the table name alone is insufficient; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 116.12 — Experiment 3: API → semantic capability ... POST /knowledge exists. This does not prove CreateKnowledgeObject. It may actually perform IndexDocument. We inspect the behavior. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 3: a POST /knowledge endpoint does not prove CreateKnowledgeObject; it may actually perform IndexDocument, requiring behavioral inspection; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 116.13 — The implementation-to-semantic mapping ... ImplementationElement→SemanticMeaning. Class↓Service↓Capability↓Domain concept. Each arrow requires evidence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the implementation-to-semantic mapping chain Class->Service->Capability->Domain concept, each arrow requiring independent evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 116.14 — Semantic extraction from tests ... Tests are particularly valuable because they often reveal the intended semantics more precisely than implementation names. shouldRejectDecisionWithoutAuthority() is strong evidence for Decision-requires->Authority.
b_rows_sample.statement: States tests are particularly strong semantic evidence, illustrated by a test name directly encoding Decision-requires->Authority.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 116.15 — Experiment 4 ... Documentation says every decision must have an authority. No test exists. Expected: E1. If code enforces it: E3. If a test verifies it: E4. This gives us a precise confidence ladder.
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 4: a documented-only rule is E1, code-enforced is E3, test-verified is E4, forming a precise confidence ladder.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 116.16 — Event extraction ... DecisionApproved, EvidenceVerified, ActionExecuted, FindingCreated. An event name is evidence of a semantic concept only if its behavior supports that meaning.
b_rows_sample.statement: States event names (e.g. DecisionApproved, EvidenceVerified) are evidence of a semantic concept only if their actual behavior supports that meaning.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 116.17 — Experiment 5 ... Event KnowledgeUpdated. What changed? If it merely means search index updated, then it is not necessarily SemanticKnowledgeUpdated. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 5: a KnowledgeUpdated event meaning only 'search index updated' is not necessarily SemanticKnowledgeUpdated; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 116.18 — Workflow extraction ... Draft→Review→Approve→Publish. This suggests lifecycle semantics. But we must determine: is this a technical publishing workflow or an authoritative governance workflow?
b_rows_sample.statement: States workflow extraction (e.g. Draft->Review->Approve->Publish) must distinguish technical publishing workflow from authoritative governance workflow.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 116.19 — Experiment 6 ... Workflow contains Review→Publish. No authority check exists. Expected: technical lifecycle established, governance lifecycle unproven. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 6: a Review->Publish transition with no authority check establishes only technical, not governance, lifecycle; result PASS.

Extends knowledgeos-semantic-core-evidence-test-model (S1013) and architecture-drift-classification-model (S1006); previews Step 117 traceability experiment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 31 distinct definitional statements, 347 files, 148 numbered steps.
a_rows_sample.statement: A full corpus scan (347 files, 148 numbered steps) locates 31 distinct definitional statements of 'Assurance', tabulated by source step/date with meaning, formal type, inputs, outputs, lifecycle, pairwise compatibility, and evidence provenance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Not one concept. Not merely overloaded terminology. Four different KINDS of thing plus one ill-formed definition: A property of a claim's justification ... A property of the ARTIFACT's form ... A risk quantity ... A structural/organisational unit ... Ill-formed
a_rows_sample.statement: The 31 statements resolve into four incompatible KINDS of thing (a property of a claim's justification — steps 140/168/211 plus the executable-vs-prose meta-claim, genuinely the same concept at different abstraction levels; a property of the artifact's FORM, a measure of the above rather than the thing itself; a risk quantity, step 092, a different concept about consequences not justification; a structural/organisational unit, steps 127 and 071, an architectural placement rather than a semantic definition) plus one ill-formed self-referential definition (step 230).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Every neighbour has a distinct, well-typed signature. Assurance has none that is not already one of them. That is the decisive test: a term with no signature of its own is not a formal term.
a_rows_sample.statement: Decisive test applied: Verification (Artifact x Spec -> Bool), Validation (K x Standard -> Assessment), Assessment (P x Evidence x Context x Policy -> Sigma), Evidence (QualifiedObservation), Backward traceability (claim -> ancestors, reachability in R_der union R_ref), and Governance compliance (Policy x Transformation -> Admissible) each already have a distinct, well-typed signature; Assurance has no signature that is not already one of these — a term with no signature of its own is judged not a formal term.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 230: Assurance = DeterministicAssurance. Step 2026-08-23 imports: "Assurance does not recursively certify itself." The corpus asserts a prohibition and then violates it 100+ steps later.
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 230's self-referential definition Assurance=DeterministicAssurance is REFUTED as ill-formed and shown to directly contradict the corpus's own later-imported Williamson prohibition ('Assurance does not recursively certify itself', 2026-08-23) — the corpus states a prohibition and then violates it 100+ steps earlier in its own numbering; JustificationStrength avoids the defect because it is a property OF a claim assigned by an EXTERNAL procedure and never certifies itself, turning the prohibition into a type constraint rather than a warning.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assurance ⟶ REMOVED from the canonical vocabulary as a formal term ... JustificationStrength(claim): Claim → OrdinalScale ... Traceability(claim): Claim → ℘(Claim) ... Risk(action): Action → OrdinalScale ... GovernanceValid(K, Γ): already defined
