a_rows_sample.anchor: context_preserved = 1.000 should never appear as 'The experiment demonstrated perfect context preservation.' It means: 'The operator was designed to preserve context.' ... A design property is not an empirical result. ... Could this number have been different if the experiment produced a different o
a_rows_sample.statement: Generalizes several audit corrections (saturation at budget 40, Z5 improperly collapsing state and observable, untested requirements 6/7, a definitional restriction-on-cross-dimension result, and context_preserved=1.000 being a design property) into a permanent methodological rule: a metric that could not have come out differently given the operator's own design is a design property, not an empirical result; proposes a litmus test ('could this number have been different if the experiment produced a different outcome?') and mandates a DEGENERATE METRICS section in every future experiment report.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Design -> Pre-register -> Calibration -> Freeze -> Analysis, with no analysis-dependent choice of estimand or population, and calibration as a separate executable that writes its gate output and exits, inspected before the analysis code is runnable. ... Observed diagnostic ⇏ new primary estimand. ..
b_rows_sample.statement: Institutionalizes the two experimental failures (KR-ZOOM-03's undirected estimand, KR-ZOOM-OUT-01's unconditional population) into a reusable experimental-governance pipeline Design->Pre-register->Calibration->Freeze->Analysis (later extended to Hypothesis->Estimand->Population->Calibration->Control->Freeze->Execution->Adjudication), with calibration executed as a genuinely separate, gated stage before analysis code becomes runnable, and two explicit safeguard rules -- an observed diagnostic must never quietly become a new primary estimand, and observed convergence across several results must never quietly become theory promotion -- both explicitly labelled research-governance safeguards, not yet KnowledgeOS theory claims themselves.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'reusable-experimental-governance-pipeline' POSSIBLY relates to 'design-property-not-empirical-result-rule' (batch B0067). Note: A reusable experimental-governance pipeline and two safeguard rules institutionalized from this experiment series' failures; extends the design-property/empirical-result discipline first recorded in S2808.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Probability measures uncertainty; information concerns what possibilities a signal eliminates; knowledge requires that the relevant information actually supports the proposition being known. ... p_i approx 1 does not imply k_i is knowledge.
a_rows_sample.statement: States Dretske's semantic-information condition (signal r carries the information that s is F iff P(F_s|r,k)=1 while P(F_s|k)<1) as grounds for a three-way non-collapse: probability, information, and knowledge are distinct, illustrated by Dretske's urn/pink-ball case (correctly believing a proposition via statistical distribution alone does not constitute knowing it); formalized as the principle that high per-claim probability does not by itself entail that a knowledge claim k_i constitutes knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: k_i = (O, d_i, v_i, t, E_i, p_i, q_i)
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends the atomic knowledge claim to a seven-field tuple k_i=(O,d_i,v_i,t,E_i,p_i,q_i) -- observation, semantic dimension, claimed value, time, evidence/information source, epistemic probability, and an explicit information-sufficiency/support status q_i -- with K_t(O)={k_1,...,k_n} as the resulting knowledge state, and reiterates that dimensionality is representation-relative rather than an intrinsic finite property of the object (a sentence maps to one or more atomic claims, not one-to-one).

a_rows_sample.anchor: a measuring instrument is a communication channel between the source and receiver. ... a voltmeter cannot simply be trusted because it displays 7 volts. Its calibration and condition matter.
a_rows_sample.statement: Models any measurement mechanism (document, sensor, API, log, interview) as a Dretskean communication channel with its own reliability/calibration conditions C_t, giving the pipeline source -> channel -> signal -> information -> determination -> knowledge (rather than source -> K directly) and making claim probability conditional on channel condition: P(v_i|E_i,C_t,O,t); offered as the theoretical foundation underneath the corpus's existing Extraction != Determination invariant.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t = (script-O, script-D, script-E, script-P)
a_rows_sample.statement: Reformulates the Knowledge State as four layers: Observation (what is being observed), Dimensions (which aspects are being considered), Evidence/information (what signals support the claims), and an Epistemic distribution (the set of per-dimension probability distributions given evidence and channel condition).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Two knowledge states could have the same total error G_t=0.3 but be completely different. ... KnowledgeOS should preserve the vector G_t=(G_1,t,...,G_n,t) before calculating any aggregate measure.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues the knowledge/epistemic gap must be preserved as a per-dimension vector G_t=(G_1,t,...,G_n,t) rather than collapsed into one aggregate scalar, illustrated by two states with identical aggregate error (0.3) distributed completely differently across dimensions (concentrated in one dimension vs. spread evenly) representing radically different epistemic situations; an aggregate G_t=sum_i w_i G_i,t is offered only as an optional secondary summary.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Z_t = (Z_truth, Z_information, Z_contract)
a_rows_sample.statement: Decomposes Zero into three named gaps rather than one: Z_truth=D(P_t,P*) (does the epistemic state match the actual state), Z_information (does the evidence actually carry the required information, a Dretskean condition distinct from mere probability), and Z_contract=D(K_t,I_t) (does the state satisfy the purpose-dependent epistemic contract) -- explicitly preserving the corpus's existing current-knowledge/information/Ideal-State distinctions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: d* = argmax_d E[Delta G_t | investigate d]. ... a_t* = argmax_a E[epistemic improvement|a] / cost(a)
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives Lord a concrete dimension-discovery objective -- choose the new dimension d expected to most reduce the epistemic-gap vector, d*=argmax_d E[Delta-G_t | investigate d] -- and Sarathi a concrete cost-normalized action-selection objective a_t*=argmax_a E[epistemic improvement|a]/cost(a), framed as deriving the architecture from the mathematics rather than the reverse.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A small signal can produce a very large epistemic reduction. ... information quantity != knowledge value
a_rows_sample.statement: States, citing Dretske's average-information-vs-particular-signal distinction (channel capacity does not determine how much a specific signal reveals), the principle 'information quantity != knowledge value': a small observation (e.g. 'port 8081 is reachable') can eliminate a very large fraction of a hypothesis space and thereby carry substantial knowledge value despite being informationally small in the aggregate sense.

a_rows_sample.anchor: World state -> Observation -> Channel -> Signal -> Information -> Probability -> Determination -> K_t, and then K_t -> gap -> investigation -> K_{t+1}.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the file's overall synthesis chain connecting the K_t hypothesis, the Ideal-vs-Actual distinction, probability, Dretske's semantic information, channel conditions, evidence, determination, Zero, Lord and Sarathi into one research direction, explicitly not yet declared a finished theory; lists five specific acknowledged remaining gaps: defining the actual state X* when it is itself unobservable, choosing the appropriate divergence D, handling dependent dimensions, distinguishing truth from confidence, and formalizing temporal identity/revision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I had not extracted everything we need from Dretske before. The earlier reading concentrated too heavily on Chapters 1-5. The decisive material for our remaining KnowledgeOS problem is actually in Chapters 7-9.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly retracts the completeness of an earlier Dretske extraction that concentrated on chapters 1-5, identifying chapters 7-9 (knowledge, belief, coding, cognitive structure, concepts) as containing decisive material for the unresolved Phi-mapping problem.

b_rows_sample.anchor: information-bearing structure -> selection/discrimination -> semantic content -> cognitive/functional state ... A cognitive system must discriminate among those pieces and select one for special treatment.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports Dretske's account that a physical/informational structure can simultaneously carry many logically or nomically nested pieces of information (if F implies G, information(F) also carries information(G)), while a cognitive system must discriminate among those pieces and select one as the content of its higher-order state -- proposed as the content of the previously near-empty semantic map Phi.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Entailed Information != Represented Knowledge. This is extremely useful for preventing knowledge explosion.
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes Entailed Information != Represented Knowledge as a principle preventing 'knowledge explosion': a statement can imply another proposition (and carry its information) without that proposition being part of what the statement means or is believed, so KnowledgeOS need not store every logical consequence of an observation as a separate knowledge atom.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Discriminate(I,R,C) -> C* where I=information-bearing structure, R=relevant alternatives, C=candidate contents, C*=selected semantic content.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a candidate DISCRIMINATE operator, Discriminate(I,R,C)->C*, grounded in Dretske's discrimination requirement, as a stronger candidate KnowledgeOS primitive than before, explicitly still [INF]/[PROP] rather than a proven primitive.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero approx relevant-alternative / requirement elimination test ... Dretske: eliminate relevant alternatives; KnowledgeOS: eliminate relevant epistemic gaps.
b_rows_sample.statement: Finds Dretske's relevant-alternatives account of knowledge (knowledge requires eliminating all RELEVANT alternative possibilities, where relevance is purpose/interest/context-dependent) structurally corresponds to KnowledgeOS's Zero(K,G,EC) test, framed as a correspondence hypothesis (not identity) and called potentially one of the most important convergences found; separately uses the same context-dependence of relevance to further justify the Ideal State's parametrization I_t(P,C).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Dimension -> Value -> Proposition -> Semantic selection, rather than Sentence = dimension.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reinforces (via Dretske's physical-structure-vs-semantic-content distinction, including his example that two semantically equivalent descriptions can correspond to different cognitive structures) the rejection of sentence-equals-dimension in favor of a Dimension -> Value -> Proposition -> Semantic-selection pipeline.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Information quantity != Semantic content, and hence Knowledge quantity != Information quantity. ... K_t = H(X) or K_t = P(X) or K_t = bits [is] fundamentally too weak.
b_rows_sample.statement: Uses Dretske's examples of signals carrying a determinate quantity of information without a determinate propositional content to establish Information quantity != Semantic content != Knowledge quantity, concluding any attempt to define K_t as a scalar measure (entropy H(X), a probability P(X), or a bit count) is fundamentally too weak.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Probability -> Support, not Probability = Knowledge. ... Dretske exposes a boundary that Kallenberg cannot solve: which proposition does the system treat as the semantic content?
b_rows_sample.statement: Cleanly divides remaining research labor between the two mathematical strands: Kallenberg/Shum answer what information is available, how uncertainty is represented, and how variables depend; Dretske answers what information is carried, what semantic content can be selected, and which alternatives matter; KnowledgeOS itself answers what knowledge state is constructed, whether it is sufficient, and what should be decided/authorized -- with probability treated as evidential support, never as knowledge itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Phi = Select o Discriminate o Interpret o Qualify o Represent ... K_t = SemanticSelect(Information(F_t,E_t), I_t, EC)
b_rows_sample.statement: Decomposes the previously near-empty semantic map Phi into a composition of five named sub-operations (Select, Discriminate, Interpret, Qualify, Represent) and proposes the research hypothesis K_t = SemanticSelect(Information(F_t,E_t), I_t, EC), where SemanticSelect is responsible for discriminating among information-bearing content, identifying relevant propositions, selecting semantic content, preserving provenance, qualifying epistemic status, and integrating the result into the current Knowledge State.

b_rows_sample.anchor: That new intermediate layer script-I_t is my strongest new proposal after revisiting Dretske. It prevents us from forcing Pi_t -> K_t directly.
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a new intermediate layer script-I_t (selected semantic content) into the unified pipeline X->Y_t->E_t->F_t->Pi_t->script-I_t->K_t->Zero->Determination->Proposal->Decision->Authorization->Action, so that the probabilistic representation Pi_t never maps directly onto the semantic state K_t but always passes through an explicit semantic-selection step -- named the strongest new proposal of this revisitation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Dretske does not give us K_t as a formal mathematical object. He also does not solve our exact atomic claim schema, KnowledgeOS revision, Zero's four-state Sigma, Governance, Authorization, our Ideal State representation, minimality of primitives, software architecture.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit negative-scope statement: Dretske does not supply a formal K_t object, the atomic-claim schema, Sigma's four-state structure, Governance, Authorization, Ideal-State representation, primitive minimality, or software architecture, and himself restricts his account largely to empirical/perceptual knowledge with acknowledged unresolved issues around necessary truths -- so 'Dretske solved KnowledgeOS' would be an overstatement; he solved part of the semantic-transition problem specifically.

Phi = Select o Discriminate o Interpret o Qualify o Represent

Note: A revision of the earlier Dretske extraction after reading the book's later chapters (7-9, knowledge/belief/coding/cognitive structure/concepts), explicitly correcting the earlier chapters-1-5-only reading as incomplete. Central discovery: Dretske gives a candidate content for the previously-almost-empty semantic map Phi:(F_t,E_t,Pi_t,S_t)->K_t via information-bearing-structure -> selection/discrimination -> semantic content -> cognitive/functional state, since a physical/informational structure can carry many logically/nomically nested pieces of information (if F implies G, information(F) carries information(G)) while a cognitive system must discriminate among them and select one for higher-order treatment -- giving Entailed Information != Represented Knowledge as a knowledge-explosion-preventing principle, and grounding a candidate DISCRIMINATE operator Discriminate(I,RelevantAlternatives,Candidates)->SelectedContent. Finds Dretske's relevant-alternatives account of knowledge (knowledge = elimination of RELEVANT alternative possibilities, relevance depending on purposes/interests/context) structurally corresponds to KnowledgeOS's Zero(K,G,EC) as an eliminate-relevant-epistemic-gaps test (a correspondence hypothesis, not identity), and independently supports the Ideal State's context-dependence I_t(P,C). Establishes Information quantity != Semantic content != Knowledge quantity (a signal can carry a determinate amount of information without a determinate propositional content), reinforcing that K_t cannot be a scalar measure (K_t != H(X), K_t != P(X), K_t != bits). Decomposes Phi = Select o Discriminate o Interpret o Qualify o Represent and proposes a research hypothesis K_t = SemanticSelect(Information(F_t,E_t), I_t, EC), introducing a new intermediate layer I_t (script-I, selected semantic content) between the probabilistic representation Pi_t and K_t so that Pi_t never maps directly onto K_t. Cleanly divides remaining research labor: Kallenberg/Shum answer 'what information is available, how is uncertainty represented, how do variables depend'; Dretske answers 'what information is carried, what semantic content can be selected, which alternatives matter'; KnowledgeOS itself answers 'what knowledge state is constructed, is it sufficient, what should be decided/authorized.' Explicitly lists what Dretske does NOT solve (a formal K_t object, the atomic-claim schema, Sigma's four states, Governance, Authorization, Ideal-State representation, primitive minimality, software architecture), noting Dretske's own acknowledged restriction to empirical/perceptual knowledge with unresolved issues around necessary truths.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 97 established KnowledgeOS as a socio-technical Organization. But resources are finite. Rigor cannot mean 'prove everything.' It must mean allocate verification and computation according to risk, value, uncertainty, and cost.
a_rows_sample.statement: Frames Step 98's central requirement: rigor cannot mean proving everything, but allocating verification/computation by risk, value, uncertainty, and cost.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 98.1 — Resources become part of the formal model ... R=(CPU,Memory,Storage,Network,Time,HumanAttention,AICompute). Cost(a)<=R for executable actions.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the resource vector R=(CPU,Memory,Storage,Network,Time,HumanAttention,AICompute) and the executability constraint Cost(a)≤R.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 98.2 — Experiment 1: unlimited verification assumption ... a proposition requires 10^9 verification operations. Available budget 10^6. Expected: KnowledgeOS cannot simply claim Verified=True. Result: PASS. The correct state is VerificationIncomplete.
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 1: a proposition requiring 10^9 operations against a 10^6 budget cannot be claimed Verified=True; correct state is VerificationIncomplete; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 98.3 — Resource limitation must not become epistemic fabrication ... Unable to verify ≠ Verified. And Not checked ≠ False.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates Unable to verify ≠ Verified and Not checked ≠ False as central to resource-constrained verification.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 98.4 — Experiment 2 ... System has insufficient compute to run a complete architecture verification. Expected: VerificationStatus=Incomplete rather than Passed. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 2: insufficient compute for full verification yields VerificationStatus=Incomplete, not Passed; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 98.5 — Verification levels ... Level_0=Unverified, Level_1=BasicCheck, Level_2=AutomatedVerification, Level_3=IndependentVerification, Level_4=FormalProof. Assurance must reflect the actual verification performed.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a five-level verification/assurance scale (Unverified..FormalProof), requiring assurance to reflect actual verification performed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 98.6 — Experiment 3 ... A component passes UnitTests. System records FormalProof=True. Expected: assurance inflation. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 3: recording FormalProof=True after only unit tests pass is assurance inflation; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 98.7 — Verification is itself a resource ... V(a) verification cost. For a critical action V(a) may be high. For a low-risk action, small. This suggests risk-based verification.
a_rows_sample.statement: States verification cost V(a) should scale with action criticality, motivating risk-based verification.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 98.8 — Risk-weighted assurance ... Risk(a), VerificationBudget(a). VerificationPriority ∝ Risk×Uncertainty.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines VerificationPriority ∝ Risk×Uncertainty, allocating more assurance to higher impact×uncertainty actions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 98.9 — Experiment 4 ... Change A: Impact=Low. Change B: Impact=Critical. Both receive identical verification effort. Expected: not necessarily wrong, but potentially inefficient and insufficiently risk-sensitive. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 4: identical verification effort for Low-impact and Critical-impact changes is potentially inefficient/insufficiently risk-sensitive; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 98.10 — Criticality ... Criticality(X): Low, Medium, High, Critical. This can influence verification, approval, redundancy, retention, monitoring, human review.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Criticality(X) (Low/Medium/High/Critical) as influencing verification, approval, redundancy, retention, monitoring, and human review.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 98.11 — Experiment 5 ... A typo in documentation: Criticality=Low. Production authorization policy: Criticality=Critical. Expected: they should not consume identical governance and verification budgets. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 5: a low-criticality typo and a critical production authorization policy should not consume identical governance budgets; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 98.12 — Cost of information ... Information(I) at cost Cost(I). Is obtaining I worth its cost?
a_rows_sample.statement: Frames information acquisition as having a cost Cost(I), raising whether it's worth paying.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 98.13 — Value of information ... VOI(I)=ExpectedDecisionImprovement-Cost(I). If VOI(I)>0, additional information may be worthwhile.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates Value of Information VOI(I)=ExpectedDecisionImprovement-Cost(I) as the criterion for seeking more information.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 98.14 — Experiment 6 ... Decision uncertainty is high. A 5-minute automated check can significantly reduce uncertainty. Expected: VOI>0. KnowledgeOS should consider performing it. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 6: a cheap, high-uncertainty-reducing check has VOI>0 and should be performed; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 98.15 — Experiment 7 ... A two-week investigation is required to reduce a tiny uncertainty in a low-impact decision. Expected: VOI<0. The investigation may not be justified. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 7: an expensive investigation for a tiny uncertainty reduction in a low-impact decision has VOI<0 and may be unjustified; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 98.16 — This gives us an important principle ... Rigor ≠ Maximum computation. Rigor = Appropriate assurance for the risk, uncertainty, and consequence.
a_rows_sample.statement: States Rigor ≠ Maximum computation; Rigor = Appropriate assurance for the risk, uncertainty, and consequence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 98.17 — Human attention is also a resource ... 10,000 alerts per day, humans can inspect 50. Alerts>AttentionCapacity. The system has failed operationally even if every alert is technically correct.
a_rows_sample.statement: States human attention is a finite resource: exceeding AttentionCapacity (10,000 alerts vs 50 inspectable) is an operational failure even with technically correct alerts.

a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 8: 1000 findings against a 20-item investigation capacity makes prioritization mandatory; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Priority(X)=f(Risk,Uncertainty,Impact,TimeSensitivity,EvidenceQuality) for allocating human attention.

a_rows_sample.anchor: T1 Compute does not imply State Change … T6 Lord proposes; Sārathi guides; the Knower/Agent commits … T7 K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,e_t) … T8 K_t=Replay(K_0,H_t)
a_rows_sample.statement: Lists eight 'foundational theorems' (T1-T8) as established fact, including T7 (a specific single-step transition-function form K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,e_t)) and T8 (a fold-style replay K_t=Replay(K_0,H_t)) — presented without proof, executable test, or governance act, in direct tension with the contemporaneous rigorous commission's finding that delta 'has no body' and 0 postconditions exist anywhere in the governed surface.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Transition \neq Overwrite ... K_{t+1} = Transition(K_t, Operation, Parameters) ... Observation, Semantic, Epistemic, Update, Comparison, Resolution, Navigation, History
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a state transition as a rule-governed operation transforming K_t into K_{t+1} (never overwriting), catalogs eight operation categories each with explicit preconditions/effects/postconditions (Observe, Detect, Parse, DiscoverDimension, DeriveProposition, Assert, Evaluate, ReEvaluate, AddEvidence, ChangeState, ReviseValue, Compare, DetectConflict, DetectGap, ResolveConflict, ResolveGap, Reframe, Prioritize, Query, Present, Preserve, Recall, Rollback).

b_rows_sample.anchor: There are actually three different concepts: Operation... Event... Transition. Operation -> Event -> StateTransition, not Operation=Transition. K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,e_t)
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the model by separating Operation (a requested transformation command), Event (a record of what actually happened), and Transition (the function mapping state+event to new state): Command -> domain validation -> Event -> delta(K_t,e_t)=K_{t+1}, an event-sourcing/DDD pattern rather than treating operations as direct mutations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Compute != Change ... Decision != Commitment ... Only committed domain events change the Knowledge State ... Zero(K_t,I_t) -> Z_t, not K_{t+1} ... Zero should not automatically mutate K.
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes Compute != Change and Decision != Commitment: analytical operations (Query, Compare, Evaluate, DetectConflict, DetectGap) must be pure computations returning results, never automatically mutating K_t; only an explicitly committed event changes the Knowledge State, reaffirming that Zero findings and Lord candidates are computed outputs, not knowledge mutations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H_t = {K_0,K_1,...,K_t} ... indexing problem... A cleaner formulation is H_{t+1}=H_t || e_t ... K_t=Replay(K_0,H_t)
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects History from a bag of full previous Knowledge-State snapshots {K_0,...,K_t} to an append-only event sequence H_t=(e_0,...,e_{t-1}), with the current state reconstructed via K_t=Replay(K_0,H_t) rather than stored redundantly -- providing auditability, reproducibility, and deterministic reconstruction as first-class properties.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Rollback should NOT mean 'set current state back'... In an immutable history model you should not rewrite history... Rollback(K3,K1) creates a new transition K3->K4 where K4 approx K1 but K4 != K1 because they have different provenance/history. Rollback != TimeTravel.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects Rollback's semantics: since history is immutable and append-only, rolling back cannot delete or revert history; instead it produces a new state K4 structurally resembling an earlier state K1 but distinct from it by provenance -- Rollback != TimeTravel, Rollback = NewStateDerivedFromHistoricalState.

b_rows_sample.anchor: T1: Compute does not imply State Change. T2: Only committed events change K. T3: History is append-only. T4: Rollback creates a new state. T5: Zero evaluates Knowledge; Zero does not constitute Knowledge. T6: Lord proposes; Sarathi guides; the Knower/Agent commits. T7: K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,e_t). T8: K_t=Replay(K_0,H_t).
b_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates the entire state-transition correction into eight named theorems (T1-T8) as the bridge from the Questions 1-14 ontology to a KnowledgeOS epistemic state machine, changing the operating vocabulary from 'operations transform knowledge state' to 'committed epistemic events transform knowledge state; operations compute, propose, or request those events'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Q18 should distinguish discovery from revision... Discovery -> Proposal -> Evaluation -> Authorization -> Revision ... Ideal State itself should have history: H^I_t, I_t=Replay(I_0,H^I_t,Pi_I). Ideal-State revision should itself be an event: I_{t+1}=delta_I(I_t,r_t).
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes symmetry between Knowledge-State and Ideal-State evolution: Ideal-State revisions must go through the same Discovery->Proposal->Evaluation->Authorization->Revision sequence as knowledge events, be recorded as an authorized IdealStateRevisionAuthorized event r_t, accumulate in an append-only Ideal-State history H^I_t, and be reconstructible via I_t=Replay(I_0,H^I_t,Pi_I) -- giving the Ideal State the same provenance/auditability the Knowledge State already has.

b_rows_sample.anchor: S_{t+1} = T(S_t, Operation, Policy, Evidence)
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies the deepest missing mathematical point: the theory has many functions (Zero, Lord, Sārathi, DiscoverDimensions, Compare, Resolve, Present) but no algebra of state transitions. Proposes S_{t+1}=T(S_t, Operation, Policy, Evidence) with required properties: determinism where required, provenance preservation, invariant preservation, authorization, reversibility/compensation where applicable, versioning — 'where the theory becomes an actual formal system rather than a conceptual ontology'.

type_signature.domain: state x operation x policy x evidence

b_rows_sample.anchor: Question \rightarrow Intent \rightarrow Context \rightarrow Knowledge \rightarrow Understanding \rightarrow NormativeAssessment \rightarrow Discrepancy \rightarrow Guidance \rightarrow Decision \rightarrow Action \rightarrow Outcome \rightarrow Observation
b_rows_sample.statement: Replaces the old Knowledge->Gap->Action loop with a longer, cyclic loop (Question->Intent->Context->Knowledge->Understanding->NormativeAssessment->Discrepancy->Guidance->Decision->Action->Outcome->Observation), formalized as a closed epistemic control loop S_{t+1}=T(S_t,Action_t,Outcome_t,Observation_{t+1}) — action produces consequences, consequences become observations, observations update knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: S_{t+1} = T( S_t, Observation, Evidence, Guidance, Decision, Action, Outcome, Policy )
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the epistemic-only transition Σ_{t+1}=ε(Σ_t,o_t) as incomplete: Chapter 3 shows transitions across knowledge, understanding, motivation, normative orientation, decision and action, giving the principal transition equation S_{t+1}=T(S_t,Observation,Evidence,Guidance,Decision,Action,Outcome,Policy) where S_t=(K_t,U_t,N_t,A_t,D_t,X_t,...). Also validates Progress = StructuredStateChange (not Progress∈[0,1]) and introduces Trajectory=(State_0,Transition_1,...,State_n) as first-class, broader than History/Provenance/Lineage; extends the epistemic lineage chain to Observation->Assertion->Understanding->NormativeAssessment->Guidance->Decision->Action->Outcome->Observation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Chapter 3 contains a feedback/cyclic system
b_rows_sample.statement: Verses 10-16's yajña cycle (Duty->Yajña->Rain->Food->Living Beings, tied back to prescribed action and Vedic direction) is read as a feedback/cyclic system, giving Action->Effect->SystemCondition->FutureAction, so ActionSystem=DynamicalSystem rather than a linear Workflow=Step1->Step2->Step3. Notes this supports event-sourced THINKING (S_n=fold(T,e_1,...,e_n)) but explicitly refuses the leap to 'therefore KnowledgeOS should use Event Sourcing' as an implementation conclusion the source does not support.

b_rows_sample.anchor: (K_t,Q,O,E,C) \rightarrow K_{t+1}
b_rows_sample.statement: Contrasts the bare LLM view y=f_theta(x) with a richer state transition (K_t,Q,O,E,C)->K_{t+1} (current Knowledge State, intent/question, observations, evidence, context), where the LLM is only one component producing the transition — 'LLM = one cognitive instrument used by the epistemic system', not 'LLM = intelligence'. Lists LLM roles as semantic parser, hypothesis generator, evidence interpreter, code generator, with KnowledgeOS deciding afterward whether output can become knowledge/an assertion, its provenance, supporting evidence, uncertainty, and conflicts — 'the missing governance layer'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Reconciliation != Knowledge and Orgasm = transition event and Knowledge = resulting epistemic state ... E_t --Reconciliation--> OrgasmEvent_t --Attribution--> K_{t+1}
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes 'orgasm' from a static balanced state to a discrete transition event (ClosureEvent) mapping an epistemic state to its successor via reconciliation and attribution, explicitly separating reconciliation from knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: +0.8 + (-0.8) = 0 ... A The evidence genuinely balances. B The evidence is contradictory. C The evidence is insufficient. D The evidence is incomparable. E ... double-counted. F ... concerns different times. All six produce something that looks like zero. ... Numeric zero != Epistemic closure.
a_rows_sample.statement: Delivers the decisive negative test: at least six distinct and non-equivalent epistemic conditions (genuine balance, contradiction, insufficiency, incomparability, dependent double-counted evidence, temporally-distinct claims) all produce apparent numeric zero, so numeric zero cannot be identified with epistemic closure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Orgasm(Q,t) <=> Closure(Q,t) and Reconciled(Q,t) and Adequate(Q,t) and Stable(Q,t) but Closure, Reconciled, and Stable are themselves currently open concepts. So we should not pretend we have solved them.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a research-hypothesis (not definition) formal criterion for an 'epistemic orgasm'/closure event conjoining four currently-open sub-concepts, explicitly flagging that none of the four is yet solved.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KR-ORGASM-2026-09-02 ... Can epistemic orgasm be operationalized as a closure event generated by proposal-challenge-reconciliation dynamics without collapsing Zero, determination, truth, or knowledge into one state? ... 15 test cases ... If they collapse into one state, the metaphor is too crude.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a falsification-oriented KR-ORGASM research track with 15 named adversarial test cases, whose success criterion is whether Balanced/Reconciled/Determined/Known/Closed remain distinguishable while dynamically linked by the closure event.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KR-ORGASM-2026-09-02 Hypothesis: A successful epistemic interaction can be modelled as a transition from unresolved inquiry through proposal, challenge, argument assessment and reconciliation to an epistemic closure event, after which a new state may contain newly attributable knowledge. Test: ... R=Reconcile(P,C,E,H,S). ... Closure(Q,R,S). ... K_{t+1}=Θ(K_t,R).
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the KR-ORGASM-2026-09-02 experiment: hypothesis that a successful epistemic interaction transitions from unresolved inquiry through proposal/challenge/argument-assessment/reconciliation to an epistemic closure event yielding attributable knowledge; test procedure computes R=Reconcile(P,C,E,H,S), evaluates Closure(Q,R,S), and derives K_{t+1}=Theta(K_t,R).

b_rows_sample.anchor: | Proposal | Challenge | Evidence | Result | ... none/none/none -> no closure ... yes/strong/sufficient+unique -> closure candidate ... yes/strong/later refuted -> retrospective revision. This last case is extremely important.
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies a 9-row test matrix over (Proposal, Challenge, Evidence) combinations mapping to closure outcomes (no closure / possible closure / closure candidate / no unique closure / retrospective revision), flagging the 'closure later refuted, requiring retrospective revision' row as extremely important.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What I would explicitly reject: Knowledge=0, IdealState=0, Facts=+n+(-n), All arguments eventually cancel, Person_A=male, Person_B=female, or Unknown=negative person. ... The 'other' is not necessarily the unknown.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit rejection list: Knowledge=0, IdealState=0, Facts=+n+(-n), 'all arguments eventually cancel', gendered Person_A=male/Person_B=female mapping, and Unknown=negative-person are all rejected; the 'other' in an epistemic interaction is not necessarily the unknown -- it may provide evidence, an alternative hypothesis, a different interpretation, or a challenge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I would therefore take the metaphor seriously enough to run the simulation, but not seriously enough to promote its equations into Theory v1.3. ... If that experiment succeeds, we may have found something important: The fundamental dynamic of KnowledgeOS may not be 'knowledge accumulation,' but repeated epistemic reproduction.
b_rows_sample.statement: Governance framing: run the KR-ORGASM simulation but do not promote its equations into Theory v1.3; if the experiment can produce a distinguishable Closure Event -> K_{t+1} without collapsing Zero/Unknown/Conflict/Reconciliation/Determination/Closure/Truth/Knowledge into one concept, the fundamental KnowledgeOS dynamic may be 'repeated epistemic reproduction' (a state encountering its own unresolved other, generating tension, undergoing examination, producing a new state on closure) rather than mere knowledge accumulation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I would not call it KnowledgeOS Theory v1.3 yet. The current state should remain KnowledgeOS Theory v1.2 [EXP/OPEN]. ... I would label the experiment: KR-ORGASM-2026-09-02 -- Epistemic Closure Event / 'Orgasm' Experiment ... and its output as a candidate v1.3 derivation, not v1.3 itself.
b_rows_sample.statement: Versioning ruling: the theory baseline remains KnowledgeOS v1.2 [EXP/OPEN]; the closure-event work is named KR-ORGASM-2026-09-02 and its output is at most a 'candidate v1.3 derivation,' not v1.3 itself, until the experiment produces sufficiently stable, non-contradictory, cross-case-supported additions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Epistemic State != Knowledge State ... Knowledge != Truth ... Claim != Assessment ... Evidence != Information ... Evidence != Knowledge ... Zero Lens != Zero Closure ... Zero != Reconciliation ... Gap != Innovation ... Unknown != Absent/Unobserved/Unobservable/Underdetermined ... Determination != closure ... Closure != knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies ~29 protected KnowledgeOS v1.2 baseline distinctions (Epistemic State!=Knowledge State, Knowledge!=Truth, Claim!=Assessment, Evidence!=Information, Evidence!=Knowledge, Interpretation!=Evidence, Determination!=Knowledge Attribution, Determination!=Truth, Proposal!=Decision, Decision!=Authorization, Authorization!=Action, Zero Lens!=Zero Closure, Zero!=Reconciliation, Gap!=Innovation, the four-way Unknown taxonomy, NotAssessed!=LowConfidence, NotApplicable!=Unknown, Conflict!=Invalidity, Model!=Reality, Representation!=Reality, evidence-quantity/weight/gain distinctions, Balanced!=truth, Balanced!=determination, Determination!=closure, Closure!=knowledge) that the experiment must not weaken merely to make itself pass.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZeroLens -> EpistemicBoundary -> Inquiry -> Proposal -> Challenge -> ArgumentField -> EvidenceAssessment -> Reconciliation -> ClosureEvent -> NewEpistemicState -> KnowledgeAttribution -> K(t+1) -> ZeroLens. ... The experiment must determine which stages are: primitive, derivable, merely representational, external, or not required.
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the initial candidate pipeline (13-stage cycle from ZeroLens through Proposal/Challenge/ArgumentField/EvidenceAssessment/Reconciliation/ClosureEvent/KnowledgeAttribution back to ZeroLens) with the requirement that each stage be classified as primitive, derivable, merely representational, external, or not required -- not assumed primitive by default.

b_rows_sample.anchor: positive arguments = +n, negative arguments = -n, reconciliation = sum = 0 ... determine whether the same numerical result can correspond to: genuine reconciliation, unresolved contradiction, insufficient evidence, incomparable evidence, dependent evidence, wrong model, multiple surviving hypotheses, temporal mismatch, irrelevant evidence, accidental cancellation. ... [NEG] Scalar cancellation is not sufficient for epistemic closure.
b_rows_sample.statement: Critical negative control: tests whether +0.8+(-0.8)=0 can correspond to ten materially different epistemic conditions (genuine reconciliation, unresolved contradiction, insufficient evidence, incomparable evidence, dependent evidence, wrong model, multiple surviving hypotheses, temporal mismatch, irrelevant evidence, accidental cancellation); if so, mandates recording [NEG] scalar cancellation is not sufficient for epistemic closure, without inventing a repair scalar.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Construct a pairwise distinction matrix: Balanced | Reconciled | Determined | Known | Closed ... A distinction counts only if you can construct a valid state where one condition holds and the other does not. Do not claim distinction merely because two words have different names.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires a 10-cell pairwise distinction matrix over five conditions (Balanced, Reconciled, Determined, Known, Closed), with the strict rule that a distinction counts only when a valid witness state can be constructed where one condition holds and the other does not -- not merely because the words differ.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Determine whether Challenge can be derived from existing operations such as: Hypothesize, Discriminate, Relate, Validate, Qualify. ... Do not use operator count alone to establish minimality. ... Likewise test Reconciliation against: Discriminate, Compare, Relate, Validate, Revise, Determine.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires testing whether Challenge and Reconciliation are each irreducible primitives or derivable compositions of existing candidate operators (Hypothesize, Discriminate, Relate, Validate, Qualify for Challenge; Discriminate, Compare, Relate, Validate, Revise, Determine for Reconciliation), explicitly forbidding operator-count alone as a minimality argument.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do NOT claim that this experiment proves the KnowledgeOS kernel. ... If kernel minimality depends on unresolved semantic equivalence, explicitly state: Kernel minimality remains blocked. Do not repeat the previous KR-2026-09-01 cardinality result as proof of minimality.
b_rows_sample.statement: Kernel test is explicitly limited: the experiment must not claim to prove the KnowledgeOS kernel, only classify newly introduced candidate capabilities (Proposal generation, Challenge generation, Argument relation, Evidence assessment, Reconciliation, Closure detection) as primitive/derivable/external/representation-only/unresolved, and must state 'kernel minimality remains blocked' if minimality depends on unresolved semantic equivalence, without repeating the prior KR-2026-09-01 cardinality result as proof of minimality.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Every major result MUST be classified as one of: [EXP] ... [NEG] ... [PROP] ... [OPEN] ... [CORPUS] ... [EXT] ... [INF]. Do not use 'established' unless it has survived the required tests and is appropriate to the evidence level.
b_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a closed seven-value verdict-category vocabulary ([EXP] experimentally supported, [NEG] falsified, [PROP] plausible proposed extension, [OPEN] unresolved, [CORPUS] corpus-supported, [EXT] external analogy, [INF] inference from established results), forbidding the word 'established' unless it has actually survived the required tests.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Never: convert metaphor into ontology without evidence, equate Zero with closure, equate reconciliation with truth, equate balance with truth, equate determination with knowledge, equate closure with permanent correctness, assume two persons are required, assume numerical +n/-n algebra is universal, claim kernel minimality from operator count, treat a simulation as proof of philosophical truth, hide contradictory results, invent missing semantics, silently repair failed definitions, promote [PROP] to [CORPUS], promote [EXP] to theorem, claim Theory v1.3 merely because a new experiment exists.
b_rows_sample.statement: Absolute research-discipline 'never' list of fifteen prohibited moves for this and by extension future experiments, closing with 'the purpose of this experiment is not confirmation. The purpose is disciplined discovery and falsification.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Ten epistemic conditions, all instantiated so the metaphor's arithmetic gives +0.8 + (-0.8) = 0 ... Nine of ten cases give sum 0, spanning three distinct (reconciled, determined, closed) signatures -- and six of them are identical on every computed predicate.
b_rows_sample.statement: [NEG] fires: across ten instantiated epistemic conditions all giving scalar sum ~0 (genuine reconciliation, unresolved contradiction, insufficient evidence, incomparable evidence, dependent evidence, wrong model, multiple surviving hypotheses, temporal mismatch, irrelevant evidence, accidental cancellation), nine of ten sum to exactly 0 but span three distinct (reconciled,determined,closed) signatures, with six of the ten cases identical on every computed predicate -- scalar cancellation is not sufficient for epistemic closure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Genuine reconciliation is not even balanced. Case 1 sums to 0.8, because a qualify relation is not a signed quantity. Balance and reconciliation are not merely non-equivalent -- they can point in opposite directions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Stronger-than-required finding: genuine reconciliation (case 1) is not even numerically balanced (sums to 0.8, not 0) because a 'qualify' relation is not a signed quantity -- balance and reconciliation are not merely non-equivalent, they can point in opposite directions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The five conditions are themselves too coarse for those six cases. What separates them is the typed relation structure and the unmet requirement -- i.e. exactly the boundary object from KR-ZERO-...-H/I. The negative control does not merely refute the scalar; it refutes any summary predicate.
b_rows_sample.statement: The negative control generalizes beyond refuting the scalar: even the five named conditions (balanced/reconciled/determined/closed/known) are too coarse to separate the six indistinguishable cases -- what actually separates them is the typed relation structure and the unmet requirement, i.e. the same boundary object already found in the Zero-Lens H/I artifacts, confirming the structure-over-projection diagnosis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Reconciliation ... DERIVABLE -- computable from the ArgumentField's typed relations alone (¬∃ a : rel(a) ∈ {unresolved, contradict}). ... Derivable ≠ mergeable: it may still be a distinct DDD responsibility.
b_rows_sample.statement: [EXP]: Reconciliation is derivable, computable directly from the ArgumentField's typed relations alone (no argument has relation in {unresolved, contradict}), introducing no power the relation typing lacks; explicitly notes derivable != mergeable -- it may still remain a distinct DDD responsibility.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Proposal generation ... derivable ... Challenge generation ... unresolved -- adversarial-negation, 2/12 derivable across representations. ... Evidence assessment ... unresolved -- warrant-assessment, 1/12. ... No capability introduced by this experiment requires new irreducible kernel power. ... Kernel minimality remains BLOCKED -- ≡_sem is undefined.
b_rows_sample.statement: Kernel test result: of six candidate capabilities, four are derivable (Proposal generation via content-generation/Hypothesize, Argument relation via relational-linking, Reconciliation and Closure-detection-as-predicate via the typed-relation predicates above) and two remain unresolved (Challenge generation as adversarial-negation, 2/12 representations derivable; Evidence assessment as warrant-assessment, 1/12); no capability requires new irreducible kernel power, but kernel minimality remains BLOCKED since semantic equivalence (=_sem) is still undefined, and the prior KR-2026-09-01 cardinality result is not reused as proof.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do NOT create Theory v1.3. The baseline remains v1.2. Two results are stable and cross-case supported and would be candidates for a future amendment -- closure is an event, not a state, and the five conditions are pairwise distinct -- but ... Insufficient for a version increment.
b_rows_sample.statement: Versioning verdict per protocol §26: Theory v1.2 remains the baseline; Theory v1.3 is NOT created. Two results (closure-as-event, and the five-way pairwise distinctness) are stable and cross-case supported and would be amendment candidates, but the ClosureEvent object is only derivable as a predicate, three boundary conditions lack a facet home, and semantic equivalence remains undefined -- collectively insufficient for a version increment.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I would preserve the current version exactly as: KnowledgeOS Theory v1.2 -- current baseline. KR-CLOSURE-2026-09-02 remains an experimental amendment candidate, not v1.3. ... Versioning should follow adjudicated theoretical change, not the number of successful experiments.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms versioning discipline: KnowledgeOS Theory v1.2 remains baseline and KR-CLOSURE-2026-09-02 remains only an experimental amendment candidate; having two potentially stable results is not itself a reason to increment the theory version -- versioning follows adjudicated theoretical change, not experiment count.
